entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 05.04.2023.
He submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the present case.
He further submits that charge-sheet has been filed and MLC report categorically stated that there is no injury at all.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Trial will take considerable time to conclude.
Upon these submissions, learned counsel prays that the applicant may be released on bail.
O n the contrary, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
FIR suggests that complainant was aged 14 years at the time of incident.
Her school record collected during investigation also confirms her age.
Statements of prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. support the fact that she was sexually abused by the applicant.
Merely on the basis of fact that MLC report does not disclose any injury, applicant cannot be released on bail.
Counsel for the applicant has relied upon two affidavits submitted as Annexure A-2.
These affidavits have been submitted by Banshrup Kol and his wife Gujarantiya Kol.

Contents of these two affidavits do not have any relevance in the context of this case because both these deponents were neither the witnesses to the incident nor they have stated a single fact about the falsehood of reported incident.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, this bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of applicant stands dismissed.
